facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He is working as a project manager at a logistics company.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work involves late hours
facts.content: Daniel stays at his desk until 10 at night. He thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes up at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Work demands during wake-up
facts.content: When Daniel wakes up at three, he has to start shipping schedules and check clients.
facts.evidence: We have to start shipping schedules, the clients, weather and forgotten something.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's physical changes
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake and he is slower.
facts.evidence: His hands shake. He's slower.

facts.heading: Father exhibits frustration
facts.content: Daniel's father gets frustrated. He is having a dream and is always being the strong one.
facts.evidence: He gets frustrated. He's having a dream and he's always being the strong one.

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel is the one who drives his father to the hospital in Leeds.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds.

facts.heading: Care responsibilities are heavy
facts.content: Daniel is responsible for all care for his father because his sister lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for her father falls on me.

facts.heading: Guilt about expressing feelings
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying anything about his situation.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it.

facts.heading: Daniel avoids sharing feelings
facts.content: Daniel does not say anything to anyone about his feelings.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone.

facts.heading: Doctor's diagnosis
facts.content: The doctor said Daniel has stress and exhaustion. Tests were normal.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion. They were all normal.

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire's feelings
facts.content: Claire said she was done watching Daniel disappear. She is very patient and makes tea.
facts.evidence: Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear. She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire's change in behavior
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause conflict
facts.content: Daniel feels the emails stop him from saying yes to plans. He has to respond to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Loss of outdoor activity
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. His legs feel like lead now.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead, and I just never went back.

facts.heading: Loss of self-identity
facts.content: Daniel feels he has lost a part of himself. Running was the one time nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: I think I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Pearson sends emails at 11 at night. Daniel answers before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an. I answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Claire hates answering
facts.content: Claire hates it when Daniel answers emails even when he is in bed.
facts.evidence: Claire hates it. I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: There is a restructuring in the spring. Daniel is afraid they will let him go.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Relief vs. guilt
facts.content: Daniel thinks he would feel relieved if he were let go. He would feel horrible about being relieved.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Moving apart from family
facts.content: Daniel moves apart from the third mess a lot, mostly.
facts.evidence: A lot, mostly. Inheritable.

facts.heading: Near heart attack experience
facts.content: Daniel slept in a colleague and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. His hand was shaking.
facts.evidence: I slept in a colleague last week, going nothing, and went and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. Hurry was going and my hand was shaking.

facts.heading: Near heart attack scare
facts.content: They thought for a second it was a heart attack but it passed.
facts.evidence: We thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Frightened about losing it
facts.content: Daniel is frightened about losing it. He fears he will end up coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day. He has started having one in the evenings.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day, and I've started having one in the evenings

facts.heading: Wine use for coping
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine sometimes. He notes it works for an hour but he wakes up anyway.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three. It works for an hour. I wake up three anyway.

facts.heading: Feeling about listing problems
facts.content: Daniel feels that listing things wrong with himself is not useful. He hears a person holding back for a long time.
facts.evidence: It doesn't feel useful. It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me. I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time.

facts.heading: Grandfather's work history
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked at the mines in New Yorkshire. His grandfather never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in New Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Daniel's reaction to his grandfather
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being there. Daniel wants to tell his grandfather he is not weak but very tired.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here. That I'm not weak. Just very tired.

facts.heading: Willingness to try small steps
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try something small between now and next week. He cannot go much left.
facts.evidence: I can't go much left. Very small.

facts.heading: Proposed small action time
facts.content: Daniel suggested fixing time in the evening when he switches off his phone for 20 minutes.
facts.evidence: Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone. Even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Proposed time for action
facts.content: Daniel suggested trying the small action around half past nine.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Planning to involve Claire
facts.content: Daniel mentioned he could make the small action a thing with Claire.
facts.evidence: I could make it a thing with Claire.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after discussing things. He feels shaky after speaking out loud.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.heading: Agreed to next session
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again next week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here.
